results.title: Lempuyang Temple Entrance Fee, Dress Code and Tips
results.content:
The entrance fee at Lempuyang Temple is 100,000 IDR ($7) per person as of 2026.

You can also take a shuttle bus from the parking area to Lempuyang Temple for 50,000 IDR ($3.50) per person round trip. Alternatively, you can walk 10 minutes uphill.

## Lempuyang Temple Dress Code

All visitors are required to wear a sarong. You can rent one at the base for 10,000 IDR. [...] Both men and women should dress modestly, covering their shoulders and knees. You may rent a sarong at the base of the temple if needed.

Disruptive Behavior: Avoid loud conversations and any behavior that may disturb the peaceful ambiance of the temple.

Remember that this is a place of worship for many, and it’s crucial to show respect. [...] Regarding the sarong for temples in general, you will get them at most temple for free or around 10,000 rupiahs (60 cents usd). If your legs are covered, usually they just give a red cloth to tie around your waist. You will have around a minute to take photos so I did some yoga poses quick. Ideally, you should cover your legs.

       Hope this info helps! Let me know if you have other questions.

       Reply

### How to Pay at Lempuyang Temple [...] ## Lempuyang Temple Dress Code

Because Lempuyang Temple is one of Bali’s sacred pillar temples, the Bali temple etiquette is strictly enforced. The rules apply to all visitors, no matter your age or gender.

### The Mandatory Sarong

Even if you are wearing long pants or a long dress, you must wear a sarong to enter the temple area. This is common at temples in Bali, but enforcement is stricter at Lempuyang.

results.title: Visiting Lempuyang Temple | Activities, Hours & Tickets
results.content:
Early Bird: Aim to arrive early in the morning to avoid crowds and experience a more serene atmosphere.
 Dress Code: Adhere to the dress code, which requires modest attire. Cover your shoulders and knees.
 Sarong Rental: If you’re not dressed appropriately, you can rent a sarong at the entrance.
 Photography: Be respectful of the sacred nature of the temple and avoid taking photos inside the main temple area. [...] By following these tips, you can make the most of your visit to Lempuyang Temple and have a truly memorable experience.

## Entrance ticket to Lempuyang Temple

 Domestic Tourists: IDR 30.000
 International Tourists: IDR 55.000

Additionally, there is a shuttle bus fee of 50,000 Indonesian Rupiah per person for a round trip.

Furthermore, the ticket price listed is for 1 person. In addition, the price of the Lempuyang Temple Entrance ticket can change at any time.

results.title: Guide to Visiting Lempuyang Temple Bali - Life With Bugo
results.content:
The rule is that your back and shoulders must be covered. Sarongs are offered to you; so it does not matter too much if you are not “properly” dressed. They are quite colourful and make for the perfect props for photos. I had read that you had to pay for them; however, they were offered free to us. There was someone collecting the sarongs afterwards.

Remember that is a Holy site after all and regardless of your faith/lack of, you must respect the culture and religion. [...] It is actually not far from Lempuyang Temple and quite beautiful in its own rights. It is possibly the closest alternative as it also overlooks Mount Agung and has the split gates. The staff there also do the iconic reflective mirror photo so you can get all that experience without having to wait hours. Entrance is also 50 000 IDR per person.

###### Sang Hyang Ambu [...] This is a really important question because not everyone has the patience to wait that long simple for a photo.

Alternatives to Lempuyang temple include:

###### Handara Gate

It is becoming a little popular now but not as intense as Lempuyang Temple. Handara gate is the entry to a luxury golf resort and tbh, it gets crowded too. Probably not as bad as Lempuyang but it is getting there. Entrance is 50 000 IDR per person which includes taking photos.
